claim: Backpressure is not a complete overload policy.
publication_wording: A bound can limit admitted work; it cannot decide which demand should wait, be refused, be retried or be discarded.
qualification: A design conclusion supported by different outcomes under the same admission bound; no isolated HTTP/2 transport-blocking experiment here.

claim: Bounded admission does not guarantee original-deadline success.
publication_wording: All primary runs respected32 occupied server slots, yet on-time completion averaged76.0–77.6% of every scheduled original.
qualification: Application ownership is bounded; do not substitute a bound on total RSS or a hard real-time execution guarantee.

claim: RETRY improved all-original deadline goodput over REJECT in this primary model.
publication_wording: Mean paired RETRY−REJECT was+1.410 percentage points; descriptive95% interval+0.889 to+2.042; five of five block differences positive.
qualification: N2880/run,2s deadline,one client/worker; paired n5 intervals are descriptive, not significance or a universal winner.

claim: Retries incurred extra attempts; normalizers matter.
publication_wording: RETRY averaged124.8 retries/run: retries/N4.333%, A/F1.0500 and A/N0.9101. Its total attempts exceeded REJECT by91.2/run because first-attempt populations also changed.
qualification: Do not call4.333% the total-attempt increase relative to REJECT; that increase is3.605%. A/N can be below1 while retries amplify sent originals.

claim: Previously refused originals sometimes completed on time after retry.
publication_wording: There were88,95,100,83,77 such originals in the five RETRY runs.
qualification: Conversion IDs are observed lifecycle facts, not the net counterfactual gain over REJECT (75,22,34,47,25).

claim: RETRY has a conditional recovery-cohort latency cost.
publication_wording: For completed originals scheduled in[24,36), RETRY per-run p95 was1.054–1.100s versus REJECT0.573–0.733s, higher in all five blocks.
qualification: Cohorts differ: RETRY n934–956, REJECT n900–932; only882–922 completed IDs are shared per pair. This is not the delay imposed on every original or a fixed-cohort causal estimate.

claim: Goodput ordering among WAIT, REJECT and DROP.
publication_wording: No clear ordering was established among these three under the primary workload.
qualification: All three paired descriptive intervals cross0; this neither proves equality nor excludes meaningful differences in other workloads.

claim: WAIT, REJECT and DROP are equivalent.
publication_wording: Do not publish an equivalence claim.
qualification: No equivalence margin/test or adequate population precision was established.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: REJECT retains less server work than WAIT.
publication_wording: REJECT’s queued+worker payload-byte-time integral was lower in5/5 pairs, mean−0.500MiB·s over39s.
qualification: This operational retention metric excludes staging, metadata, transport and allocator memory; both variants reached occupied32. It is not a demonstrated total-process-memory reduction.

claim: DROP offers a distinct operational advantage over REJECT.
publication_wording: No distinct goodput/retention tradeoff was established for DROP versus REJECT here.
qualification: All work is expendable and both policies return per-message terminal frames. DROP is not a no-response/fire-and-forget transport variant.

claim: Recovery differs between policies.
publication_wording: Some pre24-admitted server-cohort clearance comparisons differ descriptively; client backlog can persist much longer.
qualification: Cohort clearance is not whole-system recovery or a steady-state guarantee. Do not headline millisecond clearance differences as an overall recovery winner.

claim: Actual5s versus500ms deadlines change on-time completion.
publication_wording: Within the secondary runtime,5s−500ms paired U/N gains were positive in all five blocks for each policy.
qualification: These are new executions with immutable scenario deadlines, not reclassified2s primary data. Source/runtime/configuration families remain separate.

claim: RETRY improves goodput over REJECT at500ms.
publication_wording: RETRY−REJECT averaged−0.00694pp with a descriptive interval spanning0, despite additional retry attempts.
qualification: The primary2s RETRY benefit is not a universal claim across deadlines.

claim: At5s RETRY had lower goodput than WAIT in these secondary runs.
publication_wording: RETRY−WAIT averaged−0.222pp, interval−0.382 to−0.063pp.
qualification: This supports the measured negative contrast only; it does not establish a universal WAIT ranking.

claim: The anomalous500ms WAIT block is retained and materially affects summaries.
publication_wording: WAIT U counts are1485,1966,1966,1956,1944. All-five mean64.701%, median67.917%; its paired deadline-gain mean13.799pp exceeds median10.417pp.
qualification: No run was excluded or rerun. The anomalous run has363 late completions versus5–26 in other blocks; keep it visible.

claim: GC, cold start, CPU load or a particular race caused the anomalous run.
publication_wording: Its cause remains unresolved.
qualification: Timing/CPU observations are not an isolated causal diagnosis.
origin: Rejected explanation; not attributed as an established author claim

claim: Deterministic retry collision was lower than jitter in the specified model.
publication_wording: Using actual initiated retries in[12,24) and600 fixed20ms bins, deterministic collision was lower in5/5 pairs; mean relative difference−15.873%, descriptive interval−18.704 to−12.236%.
qualification: Denominator is M choose2 for M initiated retries in that window, not scheduled N or all decoded R. Mean of five relative differences, not ratio of pooled retry populations.

claim: H6’s directional prediction was contradicted in the operational study.
publication_wording: Common fixed relative backoff did not produce the predicted greater concentration under evenly staggered original arrivals.
qualification: No synchronized burst/barrier was injected. This does not refute jitter under an actual correlated herd or establish a universal counterexample to retry guidance.

claim: Jitter generally worsens overload, or variance alone caused the observed difference.
publication_wording: Do not make either causal/general claim.
qualification: Fixed100/200ms waits versus uniform[0,cap] also changes expected backoff; retry counts, client load phases and transport smoothing differ.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: B2 was chosen before any StudyB outcome could guide seed selection.
publication_wording: The original B driver stopped before any B attempt; the hashed-seed amendment was committed/frozen before B2 traffic.
qualification: This verifies the preserved record and finite-range seed check, not a human’s private A viewing history or externally trusted timestamp attestation.

claim: Eight clients preserve aggregate demand but multiply client-side capacity.
publication_wording: Eight processes each own360 IDs at10/s:80/s total, N2880. Server admission stays32/worker1; aggregate outstanding limit264 and pending256.
qualification: StudyB is not a single-client jitter replication. Eight connections/bridges and replicated ledger metadata must be disclosed.

claim: A32-slot application budget bounds whole-process RSS.
publication_wording: State the application ownership limit only; RSS peaks are sampled observations.
qualification: Transport, allocator/runtime, decoder, metadata and other allocations are separate; sampled RSS guards do not prove a hard continuous memory ceiling.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: Send duration is isolated HTTP/2 blocking or successful Send proves admission.
publication_wording: Send return is a local transport API event; end-to-end disposition requires protocol/accounting evidence.
qualification: Serialization/scheduling/instrumentation are included; successful server writes do not prove client application consumption.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: Every request is slower under RETRY, or the system fully recovered once the old server cohort cleared.
publication_wording: Use cohort-qualified latency and separate client/server backlog traces.
qualification: Different completion cohorts and unserved originals preclude either statement.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: The study proves statistical significance or a universal policy winner.
publication_wording: Five paired blocks provide descriptive, model-specific evidence.
qualification: No p-values/equivalence test/multiplicity-controlled universal decision; originals and retry pairs are not independent replication units.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: Pool all70 runs, interpolate a common500ms→2s→5s curve, or reuse Stage5 attainment curves as new deadline runs.
publication_wording: Keep primary, secondary A and secondary B2 in separate panels and comparisons.
qualification: Application runtime, clients, deadlines and observation windows differ even though each run schedules2880 logical originals.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: In-memory deduplication establishes durable exactly-once processing across crashes.
publication_wording: At most one observed worker start per logical ID in each valid run; no crash durability claim.
qualification: No durable state, restart study or external side-effect transaction was tested.
origin: Rejected extrapolation; not attributed to the authors

claim: Calculations and source/content provenance are reproducible.
publication_wording: The archived calculations, source hashes and available executable hashes reproduce; instrumentation overhead remains part of the measured model.
qualification: This is offline reproducibility, not an external-lab replication. Native secondary routing, per-attempt generation/hashing, polling and logging remain measured-model costs.

claim: The experiment used a2s gRPC stream deadline.
publication_wording: The2s primary deadline is an application-level deadline per scheduled original; the streaming RPC lasts through the workload/observation window.
qualification: Original deadlines start at the scheduled slot, include pending time, and never reset on retry. RPC context cutoff is a separate deadline.
